answer.new_information: NVIDIA's blog describes a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure, with NVIDIA earning standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity. The post gives no dollar amounts, no share percentage, no contract counts and no time period for the revenue share. The Firmus Batam figures (360 MW, up to 170,000 GPUs) are 'expected' scale for a campus, not shipments or orders, and are quoted from NVIDIA's own post. No catalog questions or stored pieces exist to update.
answer.reason: The record is a vendor party statement describing a commercial model with no sizes, timing or financial terms, and there are no catalog questions or stored pieces to attach it to. It is a pickup of strategy context rather than a number, probability or condition that moves an existing argument. Whether the revenue-share and credit-support structure warrants a new investment-exposure question (for example on NVIDIA's credit support to AI clouds and circularity of its financing) is a judgement call that the texts do not settle from this single vendor post, so no proposal is made here; the record is kept as background with the open unknowns noted: the size of the revenue share, the credit-support amounts, the period over which it applies, and whether the Firmus and Sharon AI figures are binding commitments.
